EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Indirect talks between the United States and Iran are reportedly set to resume in Pakistan, with US envoys traveling to meet the Iranian Foreign Minister, despite conflicting statements from both sides regarding the nature and willingness for direct engagement. This diplomatic effort occurs amidst heightened US military presence in the Middle East, expanded economic sanctions against Iran, and persistent cross-border hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah, underscoring significant regional instability.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran include the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) seizing the EPAMINODES ship, suspected of collaborating with the US military, for alleged violations and ignoring warnings. The Iranian Defense Ministry stated that a "significant portion" of its missile capabilities remains unused, and its forces maintained "full control over the skies of the occupied territories until the moment before the ceasefire." Iran claims to have advanced 20 years in "power factors" and tested 30 years of weapons development. Iran's Law Enforcement Chief reported uncovering a US-Israeli plan to "foment protests" via cyberspace, leading to numerous arrests. Iran's Imam Khomeini International Airport has resumed international flights, and the first Hajj pilgrims have departed for Saudi Arabia.

The internal political situation is marked by a report from the Iranian news agency Tasnim of the execution by hanging of an "agent for Israel" accused of sabotage during anti-regime protests. Conflicting reports surround the position of Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf; while Iranian sources deny his resignation from the negotiation team, Iran International and other outlets suggest he has stepped down due to internal disagreements, with Saeed Jalili or Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi as potential replacements. Senior advisor to the Leader, Mohsen Rezaei, claimed the world would soon witness the "shattering of American power." Unconfirmed reports from the New York Times state Mojtaba Khamenei is undergoing treatment for severe injuries, including prosthetics and plastic surgery, a claim an Israeli journalist suggested could be Iranian disinformation. The internet in Iran has been cut for over 1320 hours, marking its 56th day, the longest recorded internet blackout globally.

Economically, the US Treasury has imposed sanctions on a large Chinese refinery and approximately 40 shipping companies involved in Iranian oil smuggling, and blocked $344 million in cryptocurrency linked to Iran. The US stated it is unlikely to extend waivers that allowed certain countries to trade oil with Tehran. Reuters reported that Iran's perceived control over the Strait of Hormuz is causing investor fear and oil price fluctuations, with only five vessels reportedly passing through in the last 24 hours. Iran has reportedly offered to sell its shares in the Chabahar project to an Iranian company due to US sanctions.

Leadership decisions center on diplomacy: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has arrived in Islamabad, Pakistan, for a regional tour that also includes Muscat and Moscow. While the White House claims Araghchi will carry a written response to a US offer and meet US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Iran's Foreign Ministry explicitly denies any direct talks, stating Pakistan will serve as an intermediary to convey Iran's "observations." US President Trump affirmed that Iran wants to talk and is preparing an offer to meet American demands. Qalibaf warned that access to US assets could tighten if tensions escalate, urging investors to "get out while open," and denounced Israeli threats, vowing unity around the Leader.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included an overnight attack by the IAF on Hezbollah rocket launchers in Deir ez-Zahrani, Kfar Reman, and Sammaaiyeh in southern Lebanon. The IDF also struck Hamas operatives in the northern Gaza Strip, citing an immediate threat to forces. Six armed Hezbollah gunmen were identified and eliminated by Paratroopers Brigade forces in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, an operation that resulted in the death of an Oketz canine unit dog; no Israeli soldiers were injured. The IDF reported striking Hezbollah rocket launchers in Yater and Kafra, and buildings used by Hezbollah in Deir Aames, Khirbet Selm, and Touline, in response to rocket fire on Shtula. An IDF drone was shot down by Hezbollah over Tyre in southern Lebanon. The IDF foiled a weapons smuggling attempt from Jordan near the Dead Sea, capturing a smuggler and 12 handguns with drone detection. The military released footage claiming Hezbollah uses ambulances for military purposes, transporting weapons and operatives.

In terms of casualties, Nesiah Karadi, an 11-year-old girl from Bnei Brak, succumbed to her injuries from an Iranian missile attack on Passover Eve. Two IDF soldiers were moderately injured and one lightly injured in an operational accident in southern Lebanon.

Home front air defense systems were activated due to suspected drone intrusions in the Galilee Panhandle, Zarit, and Shomera; some were confirmed false alarms, while one hostile drone was intercepted, and contact with another was lost over southern Lebanon.

Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu stated he had an "excellent conversation" with President Trump, who is "pressing Iran very hard, both economically and militarily," and affirmed "we are operating in full cooperation." Netanyahu vowed to "change the face of the Middle East" and restore security to northern residents. He also revealed that he was diagnosed with early-stage prostate cancer in late 2024, underwent successful surgery and radiation, and delayed disclosure for two months to prevent Iranian propaganda.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Ground operations in Gaza included the IDF killing armed Hamas operatives in the northern Gaza Strip and continuing to destroy Hamas tunnels in the south. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers reportedly attacked Palestinians in Qusra, southern Nablus, amidst clashes, and Israeli MAGAB forces seized weapons in Abu Dis.

Casualties included several people killed and wounded in an IDF strike targeting Hamas police in Gaza City, according to the Hamas-run interior ministry. A 7-year-old child was seriously injured with a penetrating wound in an incident of violence in Rahat, and a young man sustained light injuries from stone-throwing near Duma village.

The humanitarian situation remains dire, with the World Health Organization stating that rebuilding Gaza's health system will require approximately $10 billion over the next five years. Rodent infestation is reported to be an additional health threat for displaced Gazans.

Regarding ceasefire status, Press TV reported that an Israeli strike killed Palestinian civilians, constituting a violation of the Gaza ceasefire. A Hezbollah MP also asserted that the ceasefire is "meaningless amid ongoing Israeli aggression."

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations included launching explosive-laden drones at Israeli troops in Qantara and firing rockets towards Shtula. The group claimed to have struck an Israeli army Humvee in Qantara and released footage of a precision FPV drone strike. Hezbollah shot down an IDF drone over Tyre. The killing of six Hezbollah gunmen in Bint Jbeil by IDF forces was deemed a "blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement" by Israel. Mahmoud Qamati, Deputy Head of Hezbollah's Political Council, declared that "no regional or international force can compel us to hand over our weapons." The IDF released footage purportedly showing Hezbollah using ambulances to transport weapons and operatives, undermining international law protections. Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was killed and photographer Zainab Faraj injured near Al-Tyri in what is described as an Israeli attack.

Israeli strikes targeted Hezbollah rocket launchers in Deir ez-Zahrani, Kfar Reman, Sammaaiyeh, Yater, and Kafra. Buildings used by Hezbollah in Deir Aames, Khirbet Selm, and Touline were also struck in response to rocket fire.

UNIFIL incidents included Indonesia announcing the death of an additional Indonesian UNIFIL soldier from wounds sustained in an IDF attack, bringing the total to four, and called for a UN investigation. The Lebanese Ministry of Health reported that six people were killed today in attacks in southern Lebanon, increasing the total killed since March 2 to 2,491 and the number of injured to 7,719.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Two explosive drones, attributed to Iraqi pro-Iranian militias, struck Kuwaiti military positions on the northern border, causing material damage but no casualties. Saudi Arabia condemned this violation of state sovereignty and urged the Iraqi government to address threats to Gulf states responsibly. The US has placed a $10 million bounty on Abu Alaa Al-Walai, Secretary-General of the Kataeb Sayyid al-Shuhada militia. In Karbala, Iraq, two individuals connected to al-Sadr's movement were killed or wounded in an armed attack, leading to the freezing of Saraya al-Salam activities in the city. Heavy warplane activity was observed over Mosul, Iraq, and a US F-35 reportedly flew from Israel, via Jordan, towards Iraq with its ADSB signal open. The Iraqi Coordination Framework postponed its meeting to select the next Prime Minister candidate. Meraj Iranian Airlines has resumed Tehran-Najaf-Mashhad flights after a 58-day halt. In Syria, Amjad Yusuf, a key figure in the Tadamon massacre in Damascus (April 2013), was arrested in Hama.

GULF STATES
The US military posture in the region has significantly increased, with CENTCOM announcing that, for the first time in decades, three US aircraft carrier strike groups (USS Abraham Lincoln, USS Gerald R. Ford, and USS George H. W. Bush) are operating simultaneously in the Middle East, comprising over 15,000 personnel and 200 aircraft, to support "Operation Epic Rage" and the naval blockade of Iran. Light carriers and other naval assets are also present or underway.

Diplomatically, Qatar's Emir, Tamim bin Hamad, discussed the US-Iran ceasefire agreement with President Trump and reiterated Qatar's support for Pakistan's mediation efforts. An emergency meeting of Arab Foreign Ministers, requested by Bahrain, condemned Iran's threats to close the Strait of Hormuz and held Iran responsible for any resulting damages, calling on the UN Security Council to ensure freedom of navigation. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman, Ismail Baqaee, dismissed the Arab states' joint statement as "completely rejected."

Economically, the US Treasury's extended sanctions and unlikelihood of renewing oil waivers for Iran and Russia are expected to further impact the region. Reuters reported that Iran's asserted control over the Strait of Hormuz has heightened investor anxiety, causing fluctuations in global oil prices.

Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Defense Ministry declared the Strait to be under Iran's "wise and powerful management," serving as a "control lever" for national demands. Jared Cohen of the Goldman Sachs Global Institute suggested that the Strait would never fully return to its original state, with Iran likely maintaining significant control. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated the US blockade of Iran is "going global" and that 34 ships have been turned back from Hormuz, emphasizing that the US does not need Hormuz and the "ball is in Iran's court" to agree to terms.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US-Iran Indirect Talks:** US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are traveling to Islamabad, Pakistan, for indirect talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who is carrying a written response to a US proposal. Iran officially denies direct meetings, stating Pakistan will serve as an intermediary to convey its views.
2.  **Increased US Military Presence:** Three US aircraft carrier strike groups (USS Abraham Lincoln, USS Gerald R. Ford, USS George H. W. Bush), with over 15,000 personnel and 200 aircraft, are operating concurrently in the Middle East for the first time in decades.
3.  **Expanded US Sanctions on Iran:** The US Treasury announced sanctions on a major Chinese refinery and approximately 40 shipping companies involved in Iranian oil smuggling, blocked $344 million in cryptocurrency linked to Iran, and indicated that oil trade waivers for Iran and Russia are unlikely to be extended.
4.  **Hezbollah-Israel Border Escalation:** IDF forces killed six Hezbollah gunmen in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, losing an Oketz canine unit dog. Hezbollah shot down an IDF drone over Tyre and launched explosive drones and rockets into Israel, actions the IDF labeled as "blatant violations" of the ceasefire.
5.  **Kuwaiti Border Attacks:** Two explosive drones, attributed to Iraqi pro-Iranian militias, struck Kuwaiti military positions on the northern border, causing material damage but no casualties, prompting Saudi condemnation.
6.  **Humanitarian Crisis in Gaza:** The World Health Organization estimates $10 billion is needed to rebuild Gaza's health system over five years, with ongoing concerns about rodent infestations exacerbating health threats.
7.  **Iranian Execution and Civilian Casualty:** Iran executed an "agent for Israel" accused of sabotage. Nesiah Karadi, an 11-year-old Israeli girl, died from injuries sustained during an Iranian missile attack on Passover Eve.
8.  **UK Considers IRGC Proscription:** UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced plans to present legislation to proscribe Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.
9.  **Conflicting Reports on Iranian Leadership:** Contradictory reports emerged regarding the health of Mojtaba Khamenei (severe injuries vs. disinformation) and the resignation of Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf from the negotiation team (denied by Iran, reported by other sources).

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high. While indirect talks are resuming, fundamental disagreements on the nature of these engagements, combined with an intensifying US naval blockade and expanded sanctions, create significant friction points. The substantial increase in US military assets in the region could be perceived as a preparatory measure, potentially prompting further assertive actions from Iran. The Strait of Hormuz remains an active flashpoint, with Iran asserting "complete control" and the US enforcing a blockade, raising the risk of maritime incidents. The Israel-Lebanon border is another critical flashpoint, marked by persistent Hezbollah ceasefire violations and continuous Israeli retaliatory strikes. Internally, Iran faces reports of executions and alleged foreign plots to foment unrest, alongside the longest recorded internet blackout. The US red lines appear to include preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons and ensuring freedom of navigation. Iran's red lines encompass resistance to the US blockade and any attempts to disarm Hezbollah.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** continues to frame its military operations against Iran as "self-defense" and a continuation of conflict since 1979. It is sending envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Pakistan for indirect talks, with President Trump claiming Iran desires a deal and is preparing an offer. The US Treasury has imposed new sanctions on a Chinese refinery and shipping companies involved in Iranian oil, and is unlikely to extend existing oil waivers. The US has substantially increased its military presence with three aircraft carrier strike groups in the Middle East. The Pentagon is reportedly considering options to punish NATO allies for insufficient support in the "Iran war."

**Qatar's** Emir discussed the US-Iran ceasefire with President Trump and supports Pakistan's mediation. **Saudi Arabia** condemned Iraqi militia drone attacks on the Kuwaiti border and urged Iraq to act responsibly. **Arab Foreign Ministers** collectively condemned Iran's threats to close the Strait of Hormuz and called for UN Security Council intervention.

**Germany's** Chancellor Merz suggested increasing pressure on Iran while remaining open to easing sanctions if compromises are made. **Italy's** Foreign Minister Tajani advocated for prompt resumption of talks for a peaceful resolution and stressed the importance of a secure Strait of Hormuz. **French** President Macron expressed doubts about the US's reliability as an ally and France removed climate issues from the G7 agenda to avoid confrontation with Trump.

**Russia's** Foreign Minister has expressed Moscow's readiness to support mediation efforts for a US-Iran agreement. A Russian MP claimed Iran is "undefeatable."

**China** denied US claims regarding a seized ship and called for non-interference in normal trade relations. Beijing issued a severe travel warning to Iran, advising its citizens to leave immediately.

**Pakistan** is actively facilitating indirect talks between the US and Iran, hosting Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi and preparing for US envoys, with potential for direct meetings depending on progress.

The **UK's** Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced intentions to introduce legislation proscribing the IRGC as a terrorist organization.

**Indonesia** condemned an Israeli attack in Lebanon that resulted in the death of four of its UNIFIL soldiers and called for a UN investigation.

**Argentina** renewed calls for negotiations with the UK over the Falkland Islands, while the US is reportedly reassessing its stance on British sovereignty over the islands.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions persist regarding the US-Iran talks: the White House asserts Iran initiated the request for direct talks and is bringing a written offer, while Iran's Foreign Ministry and state media explicitly deny any plans for direct engagement, stating that views will only be conveyed via Pakistan. This divergence highlights a fundamental lack of clarity on the nature and sincerity of the diplomatic process.

The health status of Mojtaba Khamenei remains unverified; New York Times reports severe injuries requiring extensive treatment, while an Israeli journalist suggests this could be Iranian disinformation to mask his potential death. Similarly, reports of Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf's resignation from the negotiation team due to internal disputes are denied by Iranian officials but widely reported elsewhere, indicating an internal power struggle or propaganda.

Unverified claims include an incident in Malard, Iran, where a 15-year-old Basiji allegedly caused casualties by accidentally firing a machine gun at a checkpoint, and a report of Iraqi Popular Mobilization Forces chanting against Iranians in Shiraz. These single-source claims require independent corroboration.

Propaganda indicators are evident across all parties. Iranian state media emphasize national unity, unspent military capabilities, and "complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz, while portraying the US-Israeli conflict as an "aggression." US statements focus on "pressure," "blockade," and Iran's need to make "wise choices." Israeli statements stress "full freedom of action" and Hezbollah's "blatant violations." Netanyahu's disclosure of cancer and justification for delaying the announcement to avoid "Iranian propaganda" also serves as a communication frame.

Reporting gaps exist concerning the specific contents of Iran's alleged "offer," the precise mechanisms and true willingness for direct engagement in the indirect talks, and the full socio-economic impact of the expanded US sanctions and continued internet blackout within Iran. The long-term implications of reported internal political struggles within Iran's leadership, such as Qalibaf's potential replacement by a hardliner, are also unclear due to the conflicting information.
